overview: The Chimu kingdom made Chan Chan a major center on Peru's north coast. Its earthen compounds, craft production and water systems show how a large city organized resources in a dry coastal environment.

items.text: Canals and irrigation supported agriculture around Chan Chan. Roads helped connect the kingdom along the northern coast.
Large walled compounds contained open courts, temples, dwellings, storage spaces, reservoirs and funerary platforms.
Earthen walls carried relief decoration with abstract patterns and human or animal subjects.
Specialized production areas supported weaving, woodworking and metalworking. These activities were part of the city's planned fabric.
Storage and water-management installations supported the city alongside agricultural land beyond its monumental center.
The kingdom reached its height in the fifteenth century before incorporation into the Inca Empire. The source used here does not establish a precise conquest year.
